title: He did everything right.
paragraphs:
He did everything right.
And still—everything fell apart.
That tension? That’s the scandal of Book of Job.

Job was called “blameless and upright” (Job 1:1).
Not fake righteous.
Not performative holy.
Real. Tested. Proven.
So why the suffering?
Here’s the part we don’t like:
Because righteousness is not a shield from pain.

In the opening of Job, heaven is having a conversation.
God points to Job’s faith.
And the accuser—Satan—fires back:
“Of course he loves You. You’ve blessed him.”
So the test begins.

Not because Job sinned.
But because his faith was worth proving.
And that’s where many of us get it wrong.

We think:
“Good life = God’s favor.”
“Hard life = God’s punishment.”
But here’s what we miss…

God was not destroying Job.
He was revealing something deeper than comfort—unshakable faith.

Job lost wealth.
Children.
Health.
Reputation.

And in the ashes, he said:
“The Lord gave, and the Lord has taken away; blessed be the name of the Lord.” (Job 1:21)

That’s not denial.
That’s surrender.
Now listen carefully:

Not all suffering is the same.
Some comes from sin.
Some from a broken world.
And some—like Job’s—becomes a stage where God displays a faith that hell cannot break.

Some scholars interpret Job as wisdom literature meant to wrestle with suffering, not just explain it.
But one truth stands clear:
God never abandoned Job.
And more than that—Job’s story whispers forward…

To another righteous man.
Perfect. Sinless.
Yet crushed.
Jesus Christ.

Jesus didn’t just suffer like Job—
He suffered for us.

Your suffering may not make sense now.
Job’s didn’t either.

But at the end, God showed up.
Not with explanations.
With His presence.
And that changed everything.

If you’re hurting and asking “Why me?”
You’re not alone.

But don’t stop at the question.
Run to the cross.

Because in Jesus, suffering is not the end of the story—
redemption is.

From ashes to glory—
because God is still writing your story.
